title: Finance & Legal Integrated Policy: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition & Billing (2028)
author: Sofia Chen
content:
Overview:

This document defines Redwood Inference's integrated finance and legal policies for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contracts and legal intake, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition and billing policies. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, product, and engineering stakeholders responsible for commercial commitments, vendor relationships, and financial reporting.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood legal entities and product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private).
- Covers budget lifecycle (planning, reforecasts, variance management), contracting lifecycle (NDAs, MSAs, SOWs), procurement thresholds and approval matrix, vendor onboarding requirements, and revenue recognition / billing rules used by Finance for month-end close and external reporting.

Principles:
- Controls must balance speed of engineering/product teams with financial and legal risk mitigation.
- Material commercial terms (payment terms, indemnities, data handling, IP) require legal review.
- Procurement thresholds are calibrated to risk and dollar value; higher-risk purchases require additional controls (security questionnaire, insurance).
- Revenue must be recognized in accordance with ASC 606 (five-step model); billing should follow the recognized pattern unless otherwise approved by Finance.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting Process

Summary:
- Annual budget approved by Board for planning; rolling 12-month forecast updated monthly by FP&A.
- Owners: FP&A (process lead), Finance Business Partners (product & GTM), department leads (cost owners).

High-level timeline (example):
1. July-September: Strategic planning and headcount model preparation for next fiscal year.
2. October: Budget submission by departments.
3. November: Executive review and negotiation.
4. December: Final budget & Board submission.
5. Monthly: Reforecast process (cut-off 3rd business day of month).

Deliverables and artifacts:
- Budget templates (revenue, COGS, OPEX broken down by function and GL).
- Headcount plan with hiring timeline and role-level rates.
- CapEx request forms and business justification.

Variance management and triggers for reforecast:
- Trigger reforecast if actuals deviate >5% of line item or if top-line guidance changes >3% quarter-over-quarter.
- Material hiring freeze or new product investments must route through Finance and CEO approval if >$500k incremental run-rate.

SLA and ownership:
- Department owners must submit monthly actuals and narrative by the 2nd business day. FP&A publishes consolidated forecast by the 5th business day.

2) Contracts & Legal Intake Process

Overview:
- All external contracts must be created from approved templates where possible. Legal is the owner for negotiating non-standard terms.

Intake and triage:
- Submit contract request via Contract Request Form (Link: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-request-form).
- Triage categories: 
  - Standard (NDA, statement of work based on template) - target turnaround 3-5 business days.
  - Commercial (new revenue contracts, resale, channel) - target 7-10 business days.
  - High-risk (data residency, unusual IP clauses, indemnity or limiting liability changes) - escalated to Legal Director; target 10-20 business days.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Requester: fills the Contract Request Form and attaches SOW/PR/PO.
- Legal: reviews commercial and legal terms; negotiates and publishes final executed agreement.
- Sales/Product/Engineering: supply commercial inputs (pricing, feature commitments, SLAs).
- Finance: approves billing terms, payment terms, and revenue accounting treatment.

Standard clause guidance (high-level):
- Payment terms: default 30 days net; exceptions require Finance approval.
- Data protection: use company-standard DPA for customer data processing.
- Liability cap: default to monetary cap equal to fees paid in prior 12 months; exceptions require Legal + CFO approval.
- Audit rights and security testing: include scope limits and notice periods.

Contract repository and tagging:
- Executed contracts must be uploaded to the central contract repository (DocStore/ContractHub) and tagged with product line, customer tier, start/end dates, auto-renewal, and revenue recognition code.

3) Procurement Procedures and Vendor Onboarding

Approval thresholds (USD):
- <= $5,000: Department manager approval.
- $5,001 - $50,000: Finance Business Partner approval + Procurement notified.
- $50,001 - $250,000: Procurement + Finance Director approval + competitive sourcing when applicable.
- > $250,000: Procurement + CFO approval + formal RFP (unless sole-source approved).

Vendor onboarding checklist (required before first payment):
- Completed vendor profile and W-9 or equivalent tax forms.
- Signed commercial agreement (NDA/MSA/SOW) or approved PO.
- Security & compliance review: either completed questionnaire, SOC 2 report, or security exception memo.
- Certificate of insurance (COI) meeting minimum vendor insurance requirements.
- Bank account details validated through secure vendor portal.

Procurement playbook highlights:
- Use competitive bids for goods/services above $50k where market alternatives exist.
- Use approved purchasing card for incidental expenses under $1,000.
- Leases and multi-year commitments require Finance and Legal review for off-balance-sheet implications and capitalization.

Exceptions and emergency procurement:
- Emergency purchases (e.g., critical infrastructure outage) may be approved by Engineering Director + Finance on-call; post-facto documentation must be submitted within 5 business days.

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing Policies

Accounting framework:
- Redwood follows ASC 606 (IFRS 15 equivalent) - apply the five-step revenue recognition model: identify contract(s), identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, recognize when performance obligations are satisfied.

Product-specific guidance:
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue in the period the usage occurs (monthly in arrears). Invoicing is monthly; deferred contract liabilities are minimal for pure usage.
- Dedicated (committed capacity): For committed contracts with a fixed monthly fee, recognize ratably over the contract term unless a distinct deliverable requires different treatment. Upfront discounts or credits are amortized over term.
- Private (on-prem / perpetual license): License fees with significant customization or implementation services must be separated into performance obligations (license vs. services). One-time implementation fees are recognized over the period services are performed unless the professional services are distinct.
- Setup / Professional services: Recognize as services are delivered unless contract indicates the service is distinct from a good or license.

Billing cadence and invoice requirements:
- Standard billing cadence: monthly in arrears for usage; monthly or quarterly for committed plans as specified in contract.
- Invoices must include: contract ID, billing period, detailed usage summary (tokens/requests/GB), unit prices, taxes, payment terms, remittance instructions, GL code(s) for internal coding.
- Payment methods supported: ACH (preferred), wire, corporate card (for smaller suppliers).

Revenue cutover and month-end procedures:
- Finance closes revenue recognition by the 3rd business day after month-end. All billing data feeds (usage, committed capacity records) must be finalized by the billing ingestion cut-off (end of day UTC on the last calendar day).
- Adjustments for billing disputes are recorded as contra-revenue and require approval by Revenue Manager and Finance Director.

Key targets and controls:
- Days Sales Outstanding (DSO) target: <= 45 days.
- Billing accuracy target: >= 99.5% (measured by invoice adjustments relative to total invoices).
- Unbilled receivables: reviewed weekly by Revenue Operations for any large contracts pending billing.

Dispute handling and credits:
- Customer raises a dispute within 30 days of invoice receipt via the billing support channel.
- Initial response SLA: 48 business hours.
- Temporary crediting or adjustments require Revenue Ops approval and documented rationale; permanent credits >$10,000 require Finance Director approval.

Tax and compliance notes:
- Sales tax and VAT: tax handling configured per customer jurisdiction; Tax team maintains nexus mapping and tax engine rules.
- Revenue recognition must consider tax implications only after accounting treatment; tax provisioning handled separately by Tax and Finance.

5) Controls, Reporting and Auditability

Controls:
- Segregation of duties for contract approval, procurement, and payment processing.
- Periodic reconciliations between billing system and general ledger (monthly).
- Quarterly internal review of vendor insurance and SOC 2 attestations for critical vendors.

Reporting:
- Monthly FP&A package: P&L by product line, variance commentary, cash runway update.
- Quarterly close pack: recognized revenue by contract type, deferred revenue roll-forward, unbilled receivables summary, and key cash metrics.

Audit readiness:
- Maintain source evidence for contract terms, signed agreements, billing records, usage logs, and bank receipts for at least seven years.
- External auditors: provide contract population files, revenue roll-forwards, and judgment memos for material contracts.

Appendices and templates (links):
- Contract Request Form: /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/contract-request-form
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (template): /confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/vendor-onboarding-checklist
- Budget Template (annual): /confluence/finance-and-legal/budgeting-and-forecasting/budget-template-annual
- Billing Invoice Template & Field Spec: /confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/invoice-template

Quick reference: GL codes (examples) -- map to Chart of Accounts:
- 4000: Hosted API Revenue
- 4010: Dedicated Revenue
- 4020: Private Deployment Revenue
- 4100: Deferred Revenue
- 5000: Cost of Revenue - Cloud GPU & Infra
- 6000: Operating Expense - G&A

Document governance:
- Policy owner: Head of Finance (Sofia Chen).
- Legal owner: General Counsel (Miguel Alvarez).
- Review cadence: Annual policy review and ad-hoc updates for regulatory or product changes.

Questions or exceptions:
- Submit policy exception requests to finance-policy@redwoodinference.com with business justification and proposed compensating controls.

This policy is intended to give operational clarity and a single source of truth for cross-functional teams executing on budgeting, contracting, procurement and revenue recognition. For detailed procedures and forms use the linked templates in the Appendices.
